drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's leniency about a removed spleen extend to a perforated spleen?
outcomeNote: A single limiting gloss on the mishna; it is attacked only in the next unit.

segments.he: נִיטַּל הַטְּחוֹל, אָמַר רַב עַוִּירָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא נִיטַּל, אֲבָל נִיקַּב – טְרֵפָה.
segments.en: § The mishna states: If «the spleen was removed» the animal remains kosher. «Rav Avira says in the name of Rava:» The Sages «taught» that it is kosher «only» when the spleen was «removed, but» if it was «perforated,» it is «a tereifa.»

moves.summary: quotes the mishna's clause, which stands in an earlier unit
moves.about: quotes the mishna's clause that an animal whose spleen was removed is kosher

moves.cueHe: אמר רב עוירא משמיה דרבא: לא שנו אלא ניטל
moves.summary: in Rava's name, limits the leniency to a removed, not a perforated, spleen
moves.about: reports Rava's limitation of the mishna's leniency about a removed spleen

edges.about: quotes the mishna's clause that an animal whose spleen was removed is kosher
reports Rava's limitation of the mishna's leniency about a removed spleen

edges.cueHe: לא שנו אלא ניטל, אבל ניקב – טרפה
edges.about: the mishna's ruling that a removed spleen leaves the animal kosher holds only for removal; a perforated spleen makes it a tereifa
